name: Food truck for events

pf.license.need: The truck's mobile food permit from the health department where it serves, with its commissary agreement; a fire inspection of the propane and cooking setup where the fire code requires one; a business license; commercial vehicle insurance. An event food permit where the local rules require one: the contract says whether the organizer or the truck files it, and by when.
pf.license.per event: Where the local rules require an event food permit, the contract says who files it and by what date.
pf.license.who holds it: The business holds the truck's permits and its commissary agreement. Each cook holds a food handler card. A certified food protection manager is on site where the health rules require one. The driver holds the license class the truck's weight needs.
pf.license.manager on site: A certified food protection manager is at each event where the health rules require one.
what to ask: The mobile food permit number and its end date
The fire inspection date, where the code requires one
Liability insurance and its amount; venues often ask to be named on the certificate
Each cook's food handler card and its end date
pf.license.how it's checked: Nothing is looked up. Rosie keeps the numbers and dates the owner gives, and the owner keeps the papers. Rosie never checks a permit, card or insurance.
pf.license.blocks going live: None from Rosie: no booking is held or refused because a permit can't be read. The owner decides what the truck offers.
pf.license.renewals: None kept by Rosie: the owner keeps the end dates and the renewals.
pf.license.insurance or bond: The owner's own liability insurance; the certificate goes to any venue that asks. Rosie never verifies it.

at the customer's place (flow B).service: Wedding or private party: guests eat, $18 a guest
at the customer's place (flow B).price: $18 a guest, 50-guest minimum ($900); an 18% service charge the business keeps (not a tip)
at the customer's place (flow B).length: 2 hours of service, plus 1 hour to set up and 30 minutes to pack up
at the customer's place (flow B).place: at the customer's site, up to 25 miles; $2 a mile after
at the customer's place (flow B).after: the rest charged to the saved card when the truck marks it done, on the final guest count

at the customer's place (flow B).service: Brewery or public night: guests buy their own
at the customer's place (flow B).price: an $800 sales minimum: if guest sales come under it, the host pays the difference on the bill after
at the customer's place (flow B).after: the bill for any shortfall, after the event

at the customer's place (flow B).service: Office lunch: meals paid by the company
at the customer's place (flow B).place: at the company's office or lot
at the customer's place (flow B).after: charged at DONE for the meals served, or the minimum

at the business (flow A).service: Wedding tasting, up to 4 guests at the commissary kitchen

pf.services.capacity: One truck, one event at a time. A crew of 2 serves up to 75 guests; 3 serve up to 150.
pf.services.nobody needs to be there: Never: food is handed to a person on the crew, who checks it.
pf.services.online: Planning calls by video or phone. Window food on a regular day is goods, sold at the window, never booked through Rosie.

before times (they set the price, length: The event date, the start time and how many hours of service
About how many guests, and whether guests eat free or buy their own
The town or ZIP, and the kind of site: a home, a venue, a park, a brewery, an office lot
Is there a level spot 40 by 12 feet, with 14 feet of clearance, for the truck to park on?
Is there power (a 50-amp or 30-amp hookup), and does the site allow a generator?
after a time is picked: The day-of contact at the site, and their mobile
The venue's vendor rules: arrival time, generator rules, and the insurance certificate it wants
The menu picks, and how many guests have a food allergy (the number only)
only on the secure page: The site's street address and any gate code
Each severe allergy, by type, for the kitchen
The venue contact who gets the insurance certificate
Age: the person booking is 18 or older
pf.questions.who may book: An adult, a business for its event, or a venue for its client. A minor never books.

stops the booking.words: A gas or propane smell, a fire, or someone hurt at the site right now
stops the booking.says: If there's a fire or a gas smell, get everyone away from the truck. If anyone is hurt or in danger, call 911 now.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

stops the booking.words: Someone has a severe allergic reaction now (trouble breathing, swelling)
stops the booking.says: Call 911 now. Use an epinephrine pen if the person has one.

safety steps, then the booking goes on.says: The truck can't promise any food is free of an allergen: the kitchen is shared. The owner calls the host before the event.

pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first. Lightning, winds over 25 mph or extreme heat stop service while they last; the contract's weather rule decides the date or the money.

before the main visit.step: The event contract, signed on the secure page
before the main visit.for: Every private or public event; Sam signs too
before the main visit.timing: At booking, before any money is taken. It has the date, hours, menu, guest minimum, the deposit, the cancel schedule, the weather rule, the site needs, and who files any event permit. Not signed in 24 hours: the booking is let go.
Sam sends it by 7 days before. Not sent: the venue may turn the truck away, which is the business's side.

before the main visit.for: Where the local rules require one for the event
before the main visit.timing: Filed by the organizer or the truck, as the contract says, by the rules' due date (often 14 days before). Not filed: the truck can't serve.

before the main visit.step: The final guest count and menu
before the main visit.timing: 14 days before, on the secure page. It sets the rest. None sent: the count in the contract stands.

prep for the reminder: Keep the truck's spot clear from 1 hour before service
Tell guests the truck can't promise allergen-free food

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The day-of contact gives the check-in code when the truck arrives to set up, 1 hour before service. A planner can get the code instead, when a mobile is given for them.
pf.visit.check-in at the kitchen: The code at the commissary desk for a tasting, or the chef types it.
pf.visit.delivery and setup: The crew sets up on the spot, runs the power, and serves for the hours booked. Nothing is left at the site.
pf.visit.food safety on the day: Hot food stays hot and cold food stays cold, by the health rules. Food out of temperature control is served or thrown away by the time limit the food code sets.
pf.visit.allergies: Allergy plates are made apart, labeled, and checked against the secure page. The truck can't promise any food is allergen-free.
pf.visit.work changes at the event: Extra guests are served from the food on hand at $18 each, as the contract says. More food or extra service time only with the customer's written yes by text, at the rate shown before booking. No yes in 10 minutes: service keeps to the booked count.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The lead cook texts DONE when service ends, with the count: guests served, meals served, or guest sales for a minimum.

starting answers: Private events: a signed contract, a $300 deposit when booking, and the rest on the saved card when the truck marks the event done (the final count sets it)
Public nights with a sales minimum: nothing taken; the host pays any shortfall on the bill after
Office lunches: a card saved, and charged at DONE for the meals served, or the 30-meal minimum
Tastings at the commissary: paid in full when booking. The planning call is free
limits: Deposit cap: from the state form
The rest is charged only after the event is done, never on a set day before it
Cancel schedule (the contract's): the deposit is kept once the date has been held 7 days; before that it's refunded
The business cancels, or the customer says no to a stand-in: a full refund
pf.money.service charge: An 18% service charge on private events is the business's own charge, shown before the yes. It's never called a tip.
pf.money.tips: A tip jar at the window is the crew's own. Off on the bill.
pf.money.tax: Sales tax on food where the state's rules tax it, from the state form.
pf.money.Rosfield's $2: Applies, as for every kind of work.

pf.messages.never in a text: Allergy details (only the count, on the secure page), gate codes, card details.

pf.staff.supervision: A certified food protection manager is on site at each event where the health rules require one.
pf.staff.who OKs what: Sam OKs every event date (one truck), any new venue, and any price made for one event. Guest count changes over 10% need his OK.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another cook with a food handler card, or a driver with the right license class. A couple who booked the owner-chef by name is asked first; nobody moves on silence.
pf.staff.who does what (the example): Rowan is the owner-chef and leads the events; Emery cooks and drives. Remy and Sasha cook at the commissary.

pf.rules.written contract: The event contract, filled in from the booking, signed by the customer and Sam before any money is taken, for every private event.
pf.rules.date hold: An event date stays saved while the contract is signed: up to 24 hours here, the owner's setting.
pf.rules.events a day: One truck: one event at a time. The owner sets any other limit.
pf.rules.final count: Due 14 days before, on the secure page. It sets the rest, charged when the event is done. Over 10% more needs Sam's OK.
pf.rules.cancel schedule: Free to cancel for 7 days after signing. After that the deposit is kept, under the contract's dated schedule. One free date change, if the truck is free that day.
pf.rules.permits: The truck's own permits; an event permit where the local rules require one, filed as the contract says.
pf.rules.distances: The fire code's distance from buildings, tents and other trucks, where it applies.
pf.rules.generators: Only where the venue and the local rules allow, in the hours they allow.
pf.rules.food safety: Hot and cold holding by the health rules; leftovers are not left with the host unless those rules allow.
pf.rules.records: Contracts, permits and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for a food truck:
food truck: Weather on the day: rain or shine; lightning or high wind stops service while it lasts. Called off: the money moves to a new date within 12 months.
The truck breaks down: a partner truck at the same price where the owner can find one, or a full refund. The event date doesn't move.
More guests than counted: served from food on hand at $18 each; past the food on hand, not served.
The final count never comes: the count in the contract stands.
The site isn't ready: the crew waits 30 minutes, then it's the customer's side.
A minimum not reached: the host pays the shortfall on the bill after.
A guest's allergy: no promise of allergen-free food; the owner calls the host first.
A cook can't come: a cook with the same skill, or a trusted stand-in if the customer agrees. A fixed-time event keeps its hours, and a certified manager must still be on the crew.
A memorial reception: no rating, no offers.
The customer moves the date: one free move, if the truck is free that day.
